articles.title: Alex Rodríguez reveals Derek Jeter's reaction during the famous Sports Illustrated photo shoot
articles.standfirst: The 1997 image became an enduring reminder of Rodríguez and Jeter's early friendship and complicated history
articles.summary: The 1997 image became an enduring reminder of Rodríguez and Jeter's early friendship and complicated history
articles.body:
Alex Rodríguez and Derek Jeter were already emerging as two of baseball’s brightest young stars when they appeared together in one of the sport’s most unusual magazine photographs.

The 1997 Sports Illustrated photo shoot in Miami Beach featured five promising shortstops: Rodríguez, Jeter, Edgar Rentería, Alex González and Rey Ordóñez.

The now-famous image showed the players shirtless, wearing baseball pants and gold chains. What was intended to showcase a talented new generation of infielders eventually became one of the strangest snapshots of their early careers.

Years later, Rodríguez looked back at the photograph with considerably less seriousness. While discussing the shoot, he joked that Jeter had been responsible for the look, saying, “I think that was Derek’s idea. We looked like Menudo. It was a dark moment.”

The comment gave the decades-old photograph another moment in the spotlight, particularly because Rodríguez and Jeter’s relationship would become one of the more complicated friendships in baseball.

In 1997, however, neither player could have known how intertwined their careers would eventually become. Rodríguez was playing for the Seattle Mariners, while Jeter was establishing himself as the Yankees’ shortstop. Both would go on to become franchise icons and among the most recognizable players of their generation.

Their friendship took a significant hit several years later after Rodríguez discussed Jeter during a 2001 Esquire interview. At the time, Rodríguez was with the Texas Rangers and suggested that Jeter had benefited from playing on talented Yankees teams and didn’t have to take on the same leadership burden as other stars.

Jeter later made it clear that the comments bothered him. He said loyalty was extremely important to him and felt that a true friend wouldn’t have made those remarks publicly.

“Those comments bothered me because, like I said, I’m very, very loyal,” Jeter said. “As a friend, I’m loyal. I just looked at it as, ‘I wouldn’t have done it.’

“And then it was the media. The constant hammer to the nail. They just kept hammering it in. It just became noise, which frustrated me. Just constant noise.”

Rodríguez eventually apologized, although he maintained that the substance of what he said was fair.

From young shortstops to Yankees teammates

Despite their complicated history, Rodríguez and Jeter eventually became teammates when Rodríguez joined the Yankees in 2004. Their relationship received plenty of attention in New York, but the pair managed to share the field for several successful seasons.

The partnership reached its high point in 2009, when the Yankees won the World Series. By then, both players had already established themselves as major figures in the sport, making their journey from the 1997 photo shoot to the Bronx particularly remarkable.

Their relationship has also evolved since retirement. Both have appeared together in baseball media, including MLB on Fox, showing that the tension that once surrounded their friendship has softened with time.

That makes Rodríguez’s recent comments about the Sports Illustrated photograph even more entertaining. Jeter may not have escaped the fashion blame, but the image has become a memorable piece of baseball history.

The original shoot was meant to introduce fans to a group of talented young shortstops, but it’s the shirtless photograph that became the lasting image.

Nearly three decades later, Rodríguez can look back and laugh at the awkward styling and youthful confidence.

articles.title: Aaron Boone showers George Lombard Jr. with love and has already moved on from Anthony Volpe
articles.standfirst: The young shortstop made everyone forget about Anthony Volpe almost immediately.
articles.summary: The young shortstop made everyone forget about Anthony Volpe almost immediately.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees roll into Camden Yards looking to lock up a series victory over the Baltimore Orioles following Tuesday's 3-1 win. A primary engine behind New York's recent momentum has been 21-year-old rookie George Lombard Jr. , who continues to reward the organization’s faith since earning his Big League call-up.

Aaron Boone raves about Lombard Jr.’s defense Ahead of Wednesday's matchup, manager Aaron Boone made no secret of his admiration for the young shortstop's transition to the majors.

“I think he’s excellent. I think he’s a great defender… Continues to show that every day he’s up here, but you know, that’s who we’ve kind of known him to be, as he’s come through the minor leagues and, it’s fun to watch him show it at this level.”

Lombard Jr. anchored Tuesday’s victory with a multi-hit performance , finishing with two hits and a run scored to anchor the bottom of the order.

Making waves around the league The rookie's immediate two-way impact has ignited social media and caught the attention of MLB analysts, who have praised his rare combination of defensive poise and offensive consistency at shortstop.

AL East playoff push The Yankees enter Wednesday holding second place in the AL East with a 70-55 record through 125 games . Following the conclusion of their series in Baltimore, New York returns to the Bronx on Friday night to open a pivotal home series against the Toronto Blue Jays .

articles.summary: Yankee Stadium hosts an American League East clash between two teams headed in opposite directions. The New York Yankees arrive as the second-best team in the AL East, with a record of 71 wins and 55 losses (sixth place in Major League Baseball), and a run differential of +89 that confirms the strength of their pitching: they have allowed only 470 runs in 126 games, one of the cleanest defensive records in the entire league.
articles.body:
Yankee Stadium hosts an American League East clash between two teams headed in opposite directions. The New York Yankees arrive as the second-best team in the AL East , with a record of 71 wins and 55 losses (sixth place in Major League Baseball), and a run differential of +89 that confirms the strength of their pitching: they have allowed only 470 runs in 126 games, one of the cleanest defensive records in the entire league.

On the other side, the Toronto Blue Jays are going through a difficult stretch . With 63 wins and 66 losses, they sit in fourth place in the AL East and carry a -49 run differential, the result of an offense that has produced just 513 runs—among the weakest among the contenders—compared to the 562 they have allowed.

On paper, the difference in quality between the two rosters is fully reflected in the market.

Yankees - Pirates: Venue and game times for this weekend

The first pitch is scheduled for this Friday, August 21, 2026, at 7:05 p.m. Eastern Time (6:05 Central Time and 4:05 Pacific Time) . The venue is Yankee Stadium, in the Bronx, New York, with a capacity of 47,309 fans. It is part of the 2026 MLB regular season.

Date : Saturday, August 22, 2026

Eastern Time : 12:35 p.m.

Central Time : 11:35 a.m.

Date : Sunday, August 23, 2026

The broadcasts of the next games at Yankee Stadium can be followed via streaming on MLB.TV on FUBO. As for the television broadcast on YES Network for New York and Sportsnet from Canada , in addition to Apple TV.

Yankees - Blue Jays roster status

The Yankees rely on a strong starting rotation : Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodón, Clarke Schmidt, Luis Gil, and Will Warren lead a pitching staff that explains that very favorable defensive differential.

In the bullpen are closers like David Bednar , Camilo Doval, and Fernando Cruz, while Austin Wells is in charge behind the plate.

Toronto balances experience and talent on its staff: Dylan Cease, Kevin Gausman, José Berríos, Shane Bieber and veteran Max Scherzer form the backbone of the rotation, backed by high-impact relievers like Jeff Hoffman, Yimi García and the crafty Tyler Rogers.

The Blue Jays' problem has not been so much on the mound as it has been with a bat that has gone cold for much of the season.

articles.title: Aaron Boone can get Cody Bellinger back, but the whole world is waiting for Aaron Judge
articles.standfirst: Yankees get a major boost with Bellinger’s return, but suffer a costly pitching loss at a critical time.
articles.summary: Yankees get a major boost with Bellinger’s return, but suffer a costly pitching loss at a critical time.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees received a major boost on Sunday with the return of Cody Bellinger , who was activated from the injured list and is set to reinforce an offense that has struggled to produce runs in recent weeks.

It wasn't all good news for New York, however. To make room for Bellinger on the roster, pitcher Ryan Weathers was placed on the 15-day injured list with a flexor muscle strain.

New York Yankees' Cody Bellinger

Bellinger's return comes at a crucial time for the Yankees, who are still dealing with several key injuries and hope to welcome back stars like Aaron Judge and Max Fried in the near future.

"I'm very excited," Bellinger said Saturday, according to MLB.com . "I feel good. I'm ready to go."

The outfielder is hitting .259 this season with 11 home runs and 53 RBIs . He had been sidelined with a hamstring strain, an injury he now says he has fully recovered from.

"As the days went on, I was pretty much running at full speed," Bellinger said. "I did defense, and more than you would probably do in a normal game. You just want to make sure you're on your feet for a long period of time."

As for Ryan Weathers , the outlook is also encouraging. Although he was placed on the injured list, the right-hander said he does not believe his season is over.

"Weathers says he doesn't necessarily think this ends his season. Says tests show elbow is fine. Says he dealt with something similar last season in MIA and it kept him out a month, but that was more severe. Says he could have kept pitching but wanted to be smart. No plan yet," The Athletic reported on X Sunday.

At 73-56, the Yankees sit second in the American League East behind the Tampa Bay Rays , but they remain firmly in the division race and hope to build momentum heading into the MLB playoffs .

articles.title: Yankees vs Astros Standings: Previous results in the season and how they enter the series
articles.standfirst: The matchup between Houston and New York in the Bronx promises to be one of the best of the week
articles.summary: The matchup between Houston and New York in the Bronx promises to be one of the best of the week
articles.body:
The 2026 MLB schedule once again brings together two organizations that rarely fail to generate sparks. This Tuesday night, the New York Yankees host the Houston Astros at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx , a matchup between historic powerhouses of the American League’s junior circuit that, however, arrive at this meeting in very different form.

Yankees vs Astros: New York in control, Houston struggling to breathe

The standings snapshot instantly explains the mood in each clubhouse. In the American League East, t he Yankees are in second place with a 73-56 record, only behind the Tampa Bay Rays (76-53).

"It is a team firmly installed in playoff position and with a positive run differential of +95 (571 scored to 476 allowed) , the best defensive mark among the big teams in the East.

On the other side, the Astros arrive with something as unusual for them as it is necessary: leaders of a very tight division . Houston leads the American League West with a 65-65 record, just one game ahead of the Texas Rangers (64-66) and with Seattle right on their heels (62-68).

Their run differential, however, raises alarms: -43 (590 scored against 633 allowed), a symptom of pitching that has bled more than it should in recent weeks .

How are the Yankees and Astros coming into this week games?

Recent form reinforces the sense of crossing paths. The Yankees are coming off a solid road trip : they won part of their series in Baltimore with 3-1, 5-3, and a commanding 6-1 victories, and put together a stretch of seven wins in nine games before splitting their most recent home series against Toronto (3-1 and then 3-4).

New York's hitting has shown power surges —like the 10-5 win over Seattle— without sacrificing its punch in close games, where its bullpen has known how to shut the door.

Houston, meanwhile, has been on a roller coaster . After a strong start to August — including an 11-2 win over Texas — the Astros have gotten tangled up: they lost series to San Diego and Seattle, and their weekend was baffling, with a humiliating 3-18 loss to the Angels followed by a doubleheader against the Athletics in which they won one game 4-0 and lost the other 3-4.

The team alternates convincing shutouts with defensive debacles, and that inconsistency is exactly what New York will want to punish.

What will the lineups be for Yankees vs Astros? Elite rotations and feared bats

If anything guarantees this matchup, it is talent on the mound. The Yankees boast a rotation loaded with elite arms : veteran Gerrit Cole (45), left-hander Max Fried (54) —signed to lead the rotation—, Carlos Rodón (55), and Dominican Luis Gil (81). For the late innings, New York has major bullpen pieces like David Bednar and Dominican Camilo Doval, a tandem capable of locking down any late lead.

Houston responds with its own artillery . Hunter Brown (58) leads a rotation that also includes Japanese pitcher Tatsuya Imai (45), Dominican Ronel Blanco (56), and the experienced Cristian Javier (53). The most feared link, however, remains the back end of the bullpen: left-hander Josh Hader (71), backed by Dominican Bryan Abreu (52), forms one of the most intimidating relief duos in the American League.

At the plate, Houston's offensive balance depends on world-class names : Cuban Yordan Álvarez (44), slotted in as the designated hitter and capable of deciding a game with a single swing, along with first baseman Christian Walker (8) and Dominican catcher Yainer Díaz (21). For New York, catcher Austin Wells (28) has established himself as a key presence behind and at the plate.

What Yankees and Astros need to reach the Playoffs

For the Yankees, every victory is ammunition in their pursuit of Tampa Bay for the top spot in the East and, above all, insurance for their postseason ticket. With the campaign entering its final stretch — both teams have already surpassed 129 games played — keeping pace against American League rivals carries double weight in the tiebreaker criteria.

For Houston, the margin is even narrower. Leading the West Division with a .500 record means that a bad stretch can cost them first place in a matter of days. With Texas just one game back, taking a series in the Bronx—hostile territory by definition—would be a statement that the pitching can hold up away from home, precisely where it has struggled the most.

articles.title: Yankees vs Astros Predictions: Who will win at Yankee Stadium and what are the odds for the game
articles.standfirst: At home, the Yankees will look to show their strength against Houston
articles.summary: At home, the Yankees will look to show their strength against Houston
articles.body:
The New York Yankees host the Houston Astros at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, and although it is a matchup of two very different stories, the scales clearly tip in favor of the home team.

Our pick at MARCA is a Yankees victory with a final score of 4-2 , with a medium-high confidence level. New York is in top form and playing at home; Houston arrives inconsistent and with a leaky defense. If you're looking for a straightforward take: the Bronx Bombers should set the tone in this series.

Analysis of the odds for Yankees vs Astros and the main bets for the game

The betting market for this matchup is not yet available, something common when the game is a day away from being played. Even so, the reading is clear from the numbers: with a +95 differential compared to Houston’s -43 , and with home-field advantage at Yankee Stadium, the Yankees should come out as consistent favorites on the moneyline, while the Run Line (±1.5 runs) would be the most contested ground.

Our recommendation when the odds open is to look for value on the New York side, and pay attention to the total runs line: with Houston's vulnerable defense , the trend toward the Over is attractive.

A New York Yankees victory is the strongest play : superior recent form, home-field advantage in the Bronx, and a run differential that is three times better than Houston’s. We recommend taking the Yankees moneyline as soon as the market opens.

Yankees -1.5 on the Run Line : If our 4-2 prediction comes through, this line pays better than the straight moneyline. Ideal for those seeking a higher return, assuming the home team wins by a margin.

Over on total runs : Houston's defense has already allowed lopsided scores (18 and 12 runs in recent losses), and the Yankees lineup is on a hot streak. The Over is a natural value avenue once the line is posted.

Prediction for Yankees vs Astros at Yankee Stadium

We expect a game in which the Yankees control the pace from the mound. The key lies in the pitching matchup : if New York sends one of its elite starters to the hill, Houston’s offense — capable of exploding, but inconsistent — will have difficulty keeping up. We reiterate our score prediction: Yankees 4-2.

We anticipate the home team striking early, taking advantage of the visitors' permissive defense, which has already allowed blowout losses this season. Alvarez is always a threat to drive in a run or even tie the game with one swing , so we do not see a shutout; hence the two runs we are giving Houston. But the Yankees' bullpen, with Bednar and Doval, has the profile to lock down a lead in the final innings.

As for the totals line, this game profile pushes toward a medium-high total number of runs. A combined score of six runs sits right in the zone where the Over 7.5 loses some appeal, but the Over 6.5 still holds value. On the Run Line, we trust the Yankees to cover the -1.5 if the game tilts the way we expect.

New York Yankees vs Houston Astros: Stats and standings in MLB

The underlying difference between the two clubs is clear. The Yankees are in second place in the American League East with a 73-56 record and are sixth in the overall Major League Baseball standings. Their offensive production (571 runs scored), combined with pitching that has allowed just 476 runs, gives them a +95 run differential, one of the strongest in the entire American League.

The Astros, meanwhile, are having an up-and-down season. They lead their division with a 65-65 record, that is, exactly .500, but in the overall standings they are as low as 14th place. Their big problem is pitching: they have allowed 633 runs, for a negative run differential of -43 . That fragility on the mound and on defense is precisely the crack New York can exploit.

In their recent stretch, the Yankees have been on fire. They swept or nearly swept important series : they took all three games against Baltimore (3-1, 5-3, and 6-1) and added quality wins like the 10-5 over Seattle and the 9-5 in Chicago. Their most recent game was a narrow 3-4 home loss to Toronto, but the overall balance of the last two weeks is clearly positive.

Houston, meanwhile, shows the roller coaster of its season. It alternates commanding blowouts—an 11-2 over Texas, a 10-7 against Seattle—with worrying collapses, such as the scandalous 3-18 suffered against the Angels and the 3-12 loss to the White Sox. Its recent finish was a double split against the Athletics (a 4-0 shutout and then a 3-4 setback).

That inconsistency, especially when the starting pitching doesn’t hold up, is their Achilles’ heel heading into the Bronx.

New York Yankees vs Houston Astros: Stats and standings in MLB

The underlying difference between the two clubs is clear. The Yankees are in second place in the American League East with a 73-56 record and are sixth in the overall Major League Baseball standings. Their offensive production (571 runs scored), combined with pitching that has allowed just 476 runs, gives them a +95 run differential, one of the strongest in the entire American League.

The Astros, meanwhile, are having an up-and-down season. They lead their division with a 65-65 record, that is, exactly .500, but in the overall standings they are as low as 14th place. Their big problem is pitching: they have allowed 633 runs, for a negative run differential of -43 . That fragility on the mound and on defense is precisely the crack New York can exploit.

In their recent stretch, the Yankees have been on fire. They swept or nearly swept important series : they took all three games against Baltimore (3-1, 5-3, and 6-1) and added quality wins like the 10-5 over Seattle and the 9-5 in Chicago. Their most recent game was a narrow 3-4 home loss to Toronto, but the overall balance of the last two weeks is clearly positive.

Houston, meanwhile, shows the roller coaster of its season. It alternates commanding blowouts—an 11-2 over Texas, a 10-7 against Seattle—with worrying collapses, such as the scandalous 3-18 suffered against the Angels and the 3-12 loss to the White Sox. Its recent finish was a double split against the Athletics (a 4-0 shutout and then a 3-4 setback).
That inconsistency, especially when the starting pitching doesn’t hold up, is their Achilles’ heel heading into the Bronx.
